text:
The Canadiens are 14-6-4 and our standings model says they are seven points ahead of their play. That is not a knock on their young core; it is a note about where the wins come from. Montreal has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and has allowed about 12 fewer goals than those chances predict, mostly thanks to rookie Jacob Fowler, whose start has put him at the top of The Hockey News' Calder Trophy tracker.

Saturday showed the other side. Fowler couldn't catch a shot and Philadelphia scored the winner in a 4-3 loss, the kind of night Sportsnet's Eric Engels described as Fowler being "human" for once.

Lane Hutson is the other headline. His pair with Noah Dobson has taken 57% of the expected goals, and he is close to Canadiens history, per Yahoo. Phillip Danault's line with Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc has driven the most play of any forward group (61% of the expected goals). Juraj Slafkovsky is running cold, with 5 points in 10 against 7.6 expected.

The injuries are piling up: Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury and Josh Anderson is also on injured reserve. Our playoff odds have Montreal at 68%. What we'd watch: whether the 5-on-5 play improves enough to stop relying on a rookie goalie.
